channel.title: Comments on: Buddha’s Truths Pertain To All Life

item.title: By: Carl Abbott
item.dc:creator: Carl Abbott
item.content:encoded:
Hi Peter,
We are innately a tribal species and so tend to align ourselves to one story or another. It’s not a sin, its biology. The Tao Te Ching goes a long way to help us peek inside nature’s way and see what is actually going on once we are able to get beyond the bias of our favorite story. That, of course, takes a lifetime. Anyway, perhaps this will elucidate the issues you raise here somewhat.

Truth is as universal as it is indescribable. Thus, Tao Te Ching begins with this disclaimer,
The way possible to think, runs counter to the constant way.
The name possible to express runs counter to the constant name.

All religions, and indeed, all spiritual paths are pointing to the same moon. Apparently only the Tao Te Ching so bluntly suggests this, not only in chapter 1, but in various ways throughout its 81 chapters.

Perhaps chapter 71’s  Realizing I don’t know is better; not knowing this knowing is disease explains our difficulty at realizing this utter universality of the human attempt to know the ‘true’ face of reality.

item.title: By: Peter
item.dc:creator: Peter
item.description: I am a bit confused as to your name. You call your group "Center Tao" and devote a considerable amount of space to teaching about Taoism, but you referenced Buddhism and other religions as well frequently. Taoism is not Buddhism (or Christianity). Zen Buddhism seems to be a blending of Taoist thought and Buddhism, but strictly speaking they are not the same. I have studied most of the world's major (and many minor) religious traditions, and it always perplexes me when I see attempts at synchronizing any of them. Just my two cents, for what it is worth (two cents?).
